name: TeamStarWolf - Plex Media Server Plex2Shell Chain (CVE-2026-96652, -96654, -96655, -96656) Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. Enterprise ATT&CK v20.0 techniques that the verified Plex2Shell record supports: the CVE and NVD records, CISA's KEV entries, Plex's security update, the researcher's write-up and an independent honeypot report. The TeamStarWolf lab run of 4 November 2026 checked versions, baselines and the fix only and ran no exploit step. Each comment names source numbers from case-studies/PLEX_MEDIA_SERVER_2026_CVES.md. Scores: 100 is a binding a primary source supports for these CVEs; 60 rests on a single press report. Scores mean evidence basis, not frequency or severity.

legendItems.label: 60: binding that rests on a single press report
100: binding a primary source supports for these CVEs

techniques.comment: Exploit public-facing application: Plex's update of 19 Oct 2026 says the chained issues let an unauthenticated remote attacker run code [9]; honeypot exploitation from 17 Oct 2026 [14]; ATT&CK page [24]. Source numbers refer to the Sources table of case-studies/PLEX_MEDIA_SERVER_2026_CVES.md.

Steal application access token: theft of the server owner's token, in Plex's CVE table for CVE-2026-96655 (19 Oct 2026) [9] and stage 3 of the researcher's write-up (16 Oct 2026) [12]; ATT&CK page [25]. Source numbers refer to the Sources table of case-studies/PLEX_MEDIA_SERVER_2026_CVES.md.

Shared modules: every .so file in the Codecs folder is loaded at startup with no signature check, per the NVD record for CVE-2026-96656 (23 Sep 2026) [4] and stage 5 of the researcher's write-up [12]; ATT&CK page [26]. Source numbers refer to the Sources table of case-studies/PLEX_MEDIA_SERVER_2026_CVES.md.

Ingress tool transfer: the transcoder fetches an attacker-hosted file (researcher stage 4, 16 Oct 2026) [12]; a miner and a packed binary downloaded on the honeypot, 17 Oct 2026 [14]; ATT&CK page [27]. Source numbers refer to the Sources table of case-studies/PLEX_MEDIA_SERVER_2026_CVES.md.

Compute hijacking: cryptocurrency miners on compromised servers, Plex's update of 19 Oct 2026 [9]; an XMRig sample on the honeypot, 17 Oct 2026 [14]; ATT&CK page [28]. Source numbers refer to the Sources table of case-studies/PLEX_MEDIA_SERVER_2026_CVES.md.

Bandwidth hijacking: proxy software routing other people's traffic through the victim, Plex's update of 19 Oct 2026 [9]; the proxy tool myawesomeproxy on the honeypot, 17 Oct 2026 [14]; ATT&CK page [28]. Source numbers refer to the Sources table of case-studies/PLEX_MEDIA_SERVER_2026_CVES.md.

Unix shell: the public proof of concept opens a reverse shell (researcher write-up, 16 Oct 2026) [12]; The Hacker News reports a shell script fetching the miner x12345 in the wild, 19 Oct 2026 (Reported) [17]; ATT&CK page [30]. Source numbers refer to the Sources table of case-studies/PLEX_MEDIA_SERVER_2026_CVES.md.
